title: Seams & Tangles Review (periodical run 5): area knots, dependency direction, ways in, rebuild readiness and change coupling — delta vs 2026-11-03 (15-commit window; the cost read landed in the "Other features" catch-all, 12 → 17 files)
description:
<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="seams-tangles" -->

**Periodical: Seams & Tangles (corrective, run 5, delta against the 2026-11-03 run).** Read how Harbour's **areas** depend on each other: where they knot, which way they point, whether each has a clear way in, how ready each is to be refactored or rebuilt behind a seam, and which areas keep **changing together**. Write a trend-framed, severity-ranked report, get an adversarial second-read, merge the report PR, mint at most \~3 one-move follow-ups, then conclude this task. **Review-only:** no code, config, guide (`scripts/code-shape/areas.json`) or doc edits beyond the report and its evidence files.

## Grounding (as found at mint time, `origin/main` = `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e`, 2026-11-04). Re-verify all of it; nothing here is a finding.

* **Repo:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour). PR and commit convention: `LIN-NNNN: <summary> (#PR)`. `ci-success` must be green before merging (`CLAUDE.md`).
* **Report convention:** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, with raw tool JSON and guide copies in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD/` (all four earlier runs used it). `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` needs a comment on this task that cites a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, plus the three second-read fields in one comment body, before Done.
* **Prior run (the baseline):** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-03.md` (run 4, LIN-4152, PR #2252, merge `be838ddd`). It measured `015aa4c6acbc008d7fa73c32beec1528b7f59511`. The series is **the committed guide at both commits** (the HEAD guide), as in runs 3 and 4. Read §1 (the four-run table and the knot-pair table), §2 (F1 to F8, N1 to N5), §3 (hubs), §4 (ways in), §6 (change coupling, the first reported run, which is the baseline for this one), §7 (guide proposals P1, P2, P3, hygiene, tests-in-guide), §8 (existing tickets, FU-1/2/3), §10 (second-read, DISAGREE, fixed in place) and §11 (the ledger, with its stable names). The 10-23, 10-20 and 10-13 reports are background.
* **This is a thin window, not a busy one.** `015aa4c6..5334c81a` is **15 commits over about 21 hours** (2026-11-03 07:55 to 2026-11-04 05:24). Two of them are the previous review reports (`aeefaf6a` Drift, `be838ddd` Seams), so 13 are code commits: LIN-4106, 4110, 4107, 4040 close-out, 4166, 4168, 4173, 4177, 4178, 4179 (one cost read, `lib/task-cost.js` deleted, `lib/cost-read.js` and `lib/cost-format.js` added), 4197, 4198 and 4202 (per-request usage records, LIN-4195 pieces 0 to 5). Production (`lib/ routes/ public/ server.js`) is 77 files, +2,674 / -991, with 9 files added and 1 deleted (verify with `git diff --shortstat` and `--diff-filter`). **A short, mostly-unchanged report is a genuine outcome here: do not pad it to match run 4's size.** The honest work is the delta on the knots that moved, the catch-all regrowth below, and the carried-forward open items.
* **Tools and guide:** `scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs <repoDir> <commit> [areaGuidePath]` and `scripts/code-shape/cochange.mjs <repoDir> <commit> --areas <path> --days 60`, both documented in `scripts/code-shape/README.md`. Neither tool changed in the window; the last commit to touch either was LIN-3881 (`856d8ae6`, 2026-10-25). **The guide changed once**, by LIN-4198 (`9cc5ff9c`): `request-usage-[^/]*` added to the "Runs & dispatch" pattern. Run both guides (`015aa4c6`'s and HEAD's) at both commits and record the guide effect apart from code movement. At mint time the old guide put `lib/request-usage-intake.js` and `lib/request-usage-store.js` in the catch-all (19 files) and the HEAD guide puts them in Runs (17 files). (zsh note: quote `"${SHA}:scripts/code-shape/areas.json"` in `git show`; bare `$SHA:s…` is a zsh modifier and silently yields the wrong file. `seams.mjs` needs `acorn`: run it from an extraction that has `node_modules`.)
* **What a quick mint-time pass saw (verify, don't quote):**
  * HEAD guide, `015aa4c6` -> `5334c81a`: **528 -> 536 files**, cross-area links **1227 -> 1262**, two-way pairs **12 -> 12**, knot group **9 -> 9** (same nine areas). The `015aa4c6` side reproduces run 4's 1227 / 12 / 9 exactly. 0 parse failures, 4 unresolved relative imports (`routes/test.js`, as in run 4), 0 non-literal dynamic imports, 0 unmapped files; `lib/` -> `routes/` imports 0 by `git grep`.
  * **The "Other features" catch-all regrew, 12 -> 17 files** (HEAD guide). The five new members are `lib/cost-read.js` (434 lines), `lib/cost-format.js` (LIN-4177/4179), `lib/founder-lookup.js` (LIN-4177), `lib/key-state.js` and `lib/key-state-holders.js` (LIN-4168). Run 4's twelve are still there (`dashboard-refresh`, `home-pipeline`, `home-row-states`, `home-rows`, `home-view`, `lineage-membership`, `live-anchor`, `row-usage`, `ruling-standing`, `subtree-index`, `task-facts-holder`, `task-state`). Of this window's code PRs, only LIN-4198 edited the guide, and its edit named its own files (`request-usage-*`), not the five above. LIN-4040, which run 4 called in-flight on these files, is **Done** now. **PR #2185 (LIN-4028,** `lib/routing-ruling.js`**, the "13th" catch-all file in run 4) is still Open**; `lib/routing-ruling.js` is not on main.
  * **Catch-all pairs grew:** Pages <-> Other **2/6 -> 8/6**, LLM <-> Other **1/1 -> 4/2**, Other <-> Runs **6/12 -> 9/15**. The new Pages -> Other edges are mostly `lib/cost-format.js` (imported by `render-kpis`, `render-workspace-kpis`, `render-run-steps`, `render-settings`, `render-effort-readout`, `ship-biscuit`, `components/decision-panel`).
  * **F1's pair moved 27/34 -> 26/35, and the apparent -1 is a relabel, not a removed dependency.** Run 4 named `model-routing-spend.js -> task-cost.js` (`buildTaskCost`) as one of the four LLM->Runs edges. `lib/task-cost.js` is deleted; the same call now goes to `lib/cost-read.js`, which the HEAD guide files under Other. Separate how much of any F1 movement is placement from real change. New real Runs-side edges to watch: `routes/proxy-runner.js` and `routes/dispatch.js` -> `lib/request-usage-intake.js` (Agent API/Web routes -> Runs, LIN-4198/4202) and the runner kit's new usage post (`lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`).
  * `lib/cost-read.js` **is a new cross-area hub in the catch-all:** it imports `lineage-membership`, `row-usage` (Other), `session-telemetry`, `dispatch-terminal` (Runs) and `llm-call-log` (LLM), and nine files import it (`workspace-kpi-stats`, `terminal-marked-task-cost`, `run-view`, `weekly-budget`, `effort-readout`, `model-routing-spend`, `routes/ship-biscuit`, `routes/proxy-compute`, `routes/settings`; count cross-area importers properly). It replaced `task-cost.js` (Runs). **LIN-4195 pieces 2 to 4 are still moving it**: LIN-4200 (In Progress) and LIN-4201 (Todo, records-first cutover, edits `row-usage`/`cost-read` fold). Judge placement as a map fact, not a code finding.
  * **Change coupling (reference for run 4's baseline):** `--days 60`, HEAD guide. At `5334c81a`: **874 changes, 400 touch 2+ areas, 76 pairs,** `shallow: false`**, 5273 unmapped files**. At `015aa4c6` the same command gives 899 / 398 / 76 / 5123, which matches run 4 §6 exactly. The two windows share 58 of 60 days, so expect almost no movement. Top pairs at HEAD: Browser code + Pages 142 (was 140), Runs + Web routes 111 (108), Browser + Web routes 107 (106), Agent API + Runs 101 (97), Pages + Web routes 99 (98). No-link pairs: **18 of 76** (19 of 76 at `015aa4c6`), 12 of them Browser code. Biggest movers are +4 each (Other + Web routes, Other + Runs, Pages + Runs, Agent API + Runs). Say plainly that this run's change-coupling delta is bounded by the window overlap and report it as such.
  * Run 4's other measurable items, to re-measure rather than assume: `window.X =` in `public/common.js` 52 (run 4: 52); route -> route file edges 53 (run 4: 53; recompute with run 4's definition); F4 `proxy-preamble` importer files 11 all-importer / 10 cross-area; `tree.js` importers 6; `task-page-loader.js` cross-area importers 7 and outbound 9; `run-controls.js` 19.
* **Carried open items from run 4 (check each against the code, not ticket state):**
  * **LIN-4154 (FU-1, Backlog, parent LIN-3490):** `fmtDuration` out of `lib/render-run-steps.js`. At mint time `lib/task-state.js:22`, `lib/task-page-loader.js:50` and `lib/render-task-page.js:58` still import `render-run-steps`. Its stated precondition (land after LIN-4106) is now met: **LIN-4106 is Done** (`300c811f`, which edited both files).
  * **LIN-4155 (FU-2, Backlog, parent LIN-3820):** `applyDefaultDispatchHarness` out of `proxy-preamble`. LIN-3738 (the wider preamble move) is still Backlog. Both follow-ups are about one day old, which is too early to say whether the purpose-parent theory held again; say that instead of judging.
  * **FU-3 (recorded only):** Providers -> `recommendation-facts` (`parentNextOf`, three edges), cross-linked to LIN-3922 (Backlog) and LIN-3923 (Backlog, "decide the LLM & prompts <-> Providers knot, now 11/4").
  * **Unparented seam tickets, all still Backlog:** LIN-3736 (hashing helpers), LIN-3737 (`collectIssueAttachments`), LIN-3738 (preamble), LIN-3555 (`RefResolutionError`), LIN-2600 (dead imports in `routes/proxy.js`), LIN-3922 (`tree.js` re-export). Say whether anything moved.
  * **Guide proposals from run 4 (nothing was adopted):** P1 (place the catch-all), P2 (`tree.js` to Task model, model routing its own area), P3 (map `^experiments/rebuild-[^/]+/` to Reports & operator tools; **left unmeasured by run 4 as a second-read leftover, so this run should measure it** as a labelled experiment, not an edit), plus the hygiene item (stop tracking `experiments/rebuild-rung7/replay/work/`, recorded not ticketed) and tests-in-guide. **LIN-4193 (Backlog, Low)** already asks for the cost modules (`cost-read`, `cost-format`, `row-usage`, `lineage-membership`) to be named into an area pattern and for `weekly-budget.js` to be renamed. Treat it as the existing ticket for that part of N1: note it, do not mint a duplicate, and say whether the whole catch-all (now 17) is a better-scoped ask than the cost slice of it. LIN-3720 is the precedent for a map-only catch-all ticket.
* **Direction rule:** the only written one is that `lib/` never imports `routes/` (LIN-675, `docs/architecture/source-map.md`). Re-confirm 0.
* **Siblings and the seams between them** (read their latest reports' sibling sections for hand-offs): **Drift & Coherence** (`drift-coherence-review-2026-11-03.md`, LIN-4153, Done) owns decisions held in several places, file-level direction, the file-level SCCs, text contracts and Simple Dispatcher's cross-repo contract, and lists Seams as owner of area-level knots, change coupling and F5 (route -> route). `lib/cost-format.js` has a browser twin `public/cost-format.js` (LIN-4179): that mirror is Drift's; the browser seam is F6 here. **Code Quality** (`code-quality-review-2026-10-20.md`) owns function size. **Stability** (`stability-review-2026-10-21.md`) owns churn and per-file change counts. **Data & Fetch Architecture**, **API Quality**, **Performance/Scale**, **Comprehension-Debt** (all 2026-10-23) and **Integration & Surface Maturity** (2026-10-21) have not run since. The cost work has its own review `cost-tracking-review-2026-11-02.md` (LIN-4126); it is not a sibling periodical, but read it for what it hands off. **Simple Dispatcher** (`JKershaw/simple-dispatcher`) is still flat CommonJS and outside what `seams.mjs` reads; say whether that still holds, and don't build a tool.
* **Parent context:** LIN-3549 (Done, code shape as a standard capability). `docs/runbooks/improvement-cycles.md` reads this report as a standing measure for the find-and-fix round ("the import map of links and knots, and change coupling").

## What to do

* **Audit the scope before executing.** Treat the scope above as a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for what is *in-remit but unlisted* (surfaces this review should cover that this scope did not name) and fold them in. Examples to check: files the guide places in the catch-all or by an over-broad regex (the five new ones above, and anything else added since); new areas or doors created this window (`lib/request-usage-*`, `lib/key-state*`, `lib/founder-lookup.js`, `lib/workspace-issues-memo.js`); wiring in `server.js` (the new `key-state` and `request-usage` wiring is not an import edge a renderer sees); the runner kit's new post to the intake (a cross-repo-shaped edge outside `seams.mjs`); the browser seam (`public/cost-format.js`, `window.X` globals, `scripts:` lists); in-flight work (LIN-4195 pieces 2 to 4, PR #2185) that is moving areas right now; and the unmapped `experiments/` subtree from run 4's second-read. A scope you could only shrink is suspect; the expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches. Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**: the wider scope changes *what you examine*, not *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome), and the follow-up bound below stays as it is.
* **Read prior runs first. This review is trend-aware.** Find and read this review's earlier reports (confirm where they are recorded rather than trusting the path above), then frame every knot as a delta against the previous run: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved, never a point-in-time snapshot. Keep run 4's stable ledger names (§11) so the next run can compare mechanically. If a name no longer fits, retire it explicitly and say what replaced it. Tell apart a change that is **placement** (a file moved between areas, or the guide edited) from one that is **code** (an import added or removed): this window's F1 delta is the live example.
* **Run the review.** Do not re-derive the dependency numbers by searching. Run `seams.mjs` at HEAD and at `015aa4c6acbc008d7fa73c32beec1528b7f59511` **with the same area guide for both runs**, so a difference is code that moved and not a map that was edited. Run both guides at both commits so the guide effect is recorded apart from code movement. Record the full commit you measured. The tool reports facts only: links between areas, knots (pairs of areas that import each other both ways, and the groups they form) and each area's entry files, plus counts of what it could not read, which you must report rather than ignore. Everything else is your judgement, written as prose with no scores and no clustering: *wrong-way dependencies* (for example run logic importing page renderers), *hub modules* that much of the code imports and that import much of it, *whether each area has a clear way in* (its entry files, and whether callers use them), *rebuild readiness per area* (could it be refactored or rebuilt behind a seam, and what stops it) and *where the areas the import graph suggests differ from the guide's names* (the "Other features" contents are the obvious place to start). Report changes since the previous report first. The guide is a guide, not a rule: propose edits to it in the report, record guide edits separately from code movement, and add no test, check or count that enforces it. The finding-classes above are **examples, not a limit. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.**
* **Read change coupling beside the import coupling.** Run `scripts/code-shape/cochange.mjs` at HEAD and at `015aa4c6…`, with the same area guide and the same `--days 60` window for both runs, and report its top pairs beside the knots, with what moved between the two and against run 4 §6's figures (which are this run's prior report). Report its counts of what it could not place (unmapped files, `shallow`) rather than ignore them. Say how much of the window the two runs share, because with 15 commits the delta is bounded by that overlap. Read a pair that changes together often yet has no link between its areas in `seams.mjs`'s output as a candidate seam: coupling the imports do not show, and a likely reason merges queue behind each other. State it as prose, with no score and nothing enforced. This is about pairs of areas only; per-file churn is the Stability Review's.
* **Mind the altitude. Do not double-flag.** This review reads the **direction and tangling between areas**. Decisions held in several places and the direction between individual files belong to the Drift & Coherence Review; function size belongs to the Code Quality Review; churn belongs to the Stability Review. Cross-link them where relevant; do not re-flag what they own.
* **Write an uncapped, trend-framed report** at `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, evidence (raw JSON from every tool run, and byte copies of both guides) in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD/`. Confirm that convention before writing. If discovery genuinely turns up no such place, put the full report in a comment on this task instead of inventing a new location. The deliverable is a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found. Finding nothing, one thing or several are all valid; do not pad, cap or invent make-work. Ground each finding in the tool output at HEAD and the source it points to, not prior prose. Close with a compact trend ledger: each knot, hub and area under a stable, descriptive name, with its severity and its delta against the previous run, plus the change-coupling top pairs as rows with their run 4 values.
* **Mint a bounded set of follow-up tasks: highest-severity only.** Create at most the top \~3 by severity in Linear (fewer is fine; zero is valid when nothing rises to that bar, and in a 15-commit window it often will). Each is well-scoped: a title, and a description that carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. A fix idea is allowed but goes under an "Unvalidated idea" heading, so later stages treat it as a hypothesis. Leave each in its default state. **Before minting, search for an existing ticket already naming the same finding** (LIN-4154, LIN-4155, LIN-4193, LIN-3922, LIN-3923, LIN-3736/3737/3738/3555/2600, LIN-4195 and its pieces). If one exists, note it in the report instead of minting a duplicate. Record EVERY finding in the report, including the ones not promoted. Err toward under-creating. Two runs of seam tickets sat unworked until a purpose-parent pulled them, so weigh whether a new ticket will be worked before minting it, and say why.
* **Shape each follow-up as one move.** Scope every minted task to a single move (for example invert a dependency, give an area one way in, or move a shared piece down a level) and the seam it would open. The move itself and where the code ends up go under its "Unvalidated idea" heading. Do not mint a task that untangles several areas at once. A guide edit (for example placing the catch-all files) is a guide proposal in the report, not a code move.
* **Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude. This is a required, structural step, not advice.** After the report and any follow-up tasks are written, and before the Done transition, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent carrying no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this same session re-reading its own report "from a cold stance") **is not accepted**; state which of Tier 1 or Tier 2 you used. Then post **one** comment on this task holding, together in a single body: `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`; `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict); and `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`. The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. **AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation**, never a reason to leave this task open.
* **Merge your own report PR.** This task owns it. Once its required CI checks (`ci-success`) are green, merge it before the Done transition. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, required checks still red) may this task conclude with the PR open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment. An open report PR is not a normal terminal state.
* **Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task, with a link to the merged report (a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, which the report gate needs). Then move this task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely; the follow-up tasks carry the actionable work forward.
* **Stay review-only.** Producing the report changes no code, config, guide or secrets, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's own deliverable.

---

## Research notes: Seams & Tangles run 5 (LIN-4208)

**Re-grounded at `origin/main` = `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e` (unchanged since the ticket was created; `git log --since=2026-11-04T07:46:14Z origin/main` is empty).** Baseline `015aa4c6acbc008d7fa73c32beec1528b7f59511`. 15 commits; production diff `lib routes public server.js` = 77 files, +2,674 / −991. Added: `lib/cost-format.js`, `cost-read.js`, `founder-lookup.js`, `key-state.js`, `key-state-holders.js`, `request-usage-intake.js`, `request-usage-store.js`, `workspace-issues-memo.js`, `public/cost-format.js`. Deleted: `lib/task-cost.js`. **Every grounding figure in the description reproduced exactly.** I found one mint-time slip and several items it did not list (marked **NEW** below).

### 0. How it was measured (so the report stage can regenerate it byte for byte)
From the LinearViewer repo root, with the guides extracted using `git show "<sha>:scripts/code-shape/areas.json"` (quoted, because zsh `:s` modifiers bit me once and returned a wrong file):
- `seams.mjs . <commit> <guide>` × {015aa4c6, 5334c81a} × {old guide, HEAD guide}: 4 runs.
- `cochange.mjs . <commit> --areas <guide> --days 60` × the same 4.
- File-level edges come from run 4's committed generator, `node docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-03/edge-dump.mjs . <commit> <guide>`. Witness: its cross-area count equals the seams `links` total (1227 and 1262, checked).
- Labelled experiments, not guide edits: **P3** (`^experiments/rebuild-[^/]+/` added to Reports & operator tools) on cochange at both commits and on seams at HEAD. **P1b**: run 4's P1 mapping for the 12 files, plus the 5 new ones (cost-read and founder-lookup → Runs; cost-format, key-state and key-state-holders → Platform), run with seams at both commits.

### 1. Four-run table (seams)
| code \ guide | old guide (015aa4c6) | HEAD guide (5334c81a) |
|---|---|---|
| 015aa4c6 | 528 files · 1227 links · 12 pairs · group 9 · Other 12 | **identical** (the guide edit names files that do not exist yet) |
| 5334c81a | 536 · 1262 · 12 · 9 · **Other 19** | 536 · 1262 · 12 · 9 · **Other 17** |

- **Guide effect:** only at HEAD, and only the placement of `request-usage-intake.js` and `request-usage-store.js` (Other under the old guide, Runs under HEAD). Links and pairs do not change. Every run had 0 parse failures, 4 unresolved relative imports (`routes/test.js`), 0 non-literal dynamic imports and 0 unmapped files. `lib/`→`routes/` imports: 0 at both commits (`git grep`).
- **Area file counts (HEAD guide, old → new):** Other 12→17; Runs 101→102 (+2 request-usage, −task-cost); Auth 63→64 (`workspace-issues-memo.js`); Browser 42→43 (`public/cost-format.js`). Every other area is unchanged.

### 2. Per-layer audit (brief + source)
**L1 "Other features" catch-all (N1). Worsened, 12→17.** The five new files and how each is reached (edge dump):
- `cost-read.js`: 9 cross-area importers from 5 areas (`effort-readout`, `model-routing-spend`, `run-view`, `terminal-marked-task-cost`, `weekly-budget`, `workspace-kpi-stats`, `routes/proxy-compute`, `routes/settings`, `routes/ship-biscuit`). It imports `dispatch-terminal` and `session-telemetry` (Runs), `llm-call-log` (LLM) and `utils/time`, at `lib/cost-read.js:28-33`. It is **bidirectional with Runs**, as `task-cost.js` was.
- `cost-format.js`: a leaf with 7 importers (6 Pages files plus `ship-biscuit`). It cannot knot.
- `founder-lookup.js`: imported by `workspace-kpi-stats` (Reports) and `server.js:155`; imports `dispatch-store` (Runs).
- `key-state.js` and `key-state-holders.js`: imported only by `server.js:167-168`; no outbound imports. They are wiring-only plumbing.

Pair movement: Pages↔Other 2/6→**8/6** (all six new edges go to `cost-format`). LLM↔Other 1/1→**4/2**. Other↔Runs 6/12→**9/15**. Also: Wiring→Other 5→8, Web routes→Other 3→6, Agent API→Other 1→2, and **NEW Reports→Other 0→2** (`workspace-kpi-stats` → `cost-read` and `founder-lookup`). **Labelling vs code (P1b spike):** placing all 17 files removes the catch-all (Other 0, 12 pairs, group **8**, 1239 links), the same shape as run 4's P1 (group 8). So the three Other pairs are labelling. The real wrong-way code is still the three files run 4 named: `task-state.js:21-22` (→`run-view`, →`render-run-steps`), `home-row-states` and `subtree-index`.
